notes.text: The live opening treats nu=2, with K^g={P} and I=K minus K^g a union of two orbits. It calls g a universal automorphism of Sigma minus I and says that P is a fixed point. These assertions were transcribed, not mathematically checked.

The canceled calculation uses rho=lambda+1/lambda, then the written quadratic and radical expressions. Its cancelled state and local revisions are retained. Reader C performed no algebra; the main reader’s limited checks are recorded below as S035-C01–C03.

The live configuration paragraph says that this case has moduli, describes square configurations, asks whether one construction is case 1°, and places P among the six vertices of an associated octahedron in the tetrahedral case. These are manuscript claims, not verified conclusions.

The last paragraph asserts that the finite-order antiautomorphism under discussion has order 2 and corresponds to a real structure, then distinguishes fixed-set cardinalities 1, 3 and 5. This argument was not checked.

The large framed calculation is canceled by long diagonal strokes. Local deletions inside it are separately retained: donnée par, lambda=, the radicals after J, the first changeant, the quadratic-root formula and les. The two inserted mu-set formulas remain part of the canceled draft.

The first reading du notre point de vue is retained with de as an alternative; grammatical expectation does not decide the compressed last letter. Similarly, the canceled final prose remains tentative rather than being completed into a coherent argument.

The initial interlinear Dans ce cas and the insertion after P est are present. The latter is read un de with un as an alternative; the witnesses do not justify supplying ses. A separate crossed baseline word remains tentatively un.

Reader C initially favored il and a resolved équilatéral. Root comparison of the same saved crops did not securely exclude sigma or certify every internal letter of équilatéral, so both doubts are retained. Root also identified the possible opening parenthesis of the case note as an insertion-leader ambiguity.

Both drawings preserve open contours and visible gaps. The lower drawing includes two edge points in addition to its four vertex points and P, plus a dotted oblique slant. No arrowhead is supplied for the detached upper-left curved stroke.
No manuscript date appears on this sheet. The top number 2 and bottom foliation 34 are transcribed separately; neither number is used to infer a date.

Whole-page layout and both native overlapping halves were read once. All 25 saved crops were visually inspected; each PNG was successfully loaded before a same-pixel JPEG transport copy was made. The added canceled_comme rectangle is the first crop for that distinct word place, which earlier rectangles clipped. No OCR, research or TeX compilation was used.

For nonzero lambda, rho=lambda+lambda^{-1} gives lambda^2-rho lambda+1=0 by multiplication by lambda. Also rho-2=(lambda-1)^2/lambda, so lambda!=1 is equivalent to rho!=2 over a field. In characteristic0, lambda=-1 gives rho=-2 and is not excluded. This verifies the inserted inequality without changing the cancelled draft.

For lambda^2-rho lambda+1 in characteristic0 the discriminant is rho^2-4 and the quadratic formula gives (rho±sqrt(rho^2-4))/2. Substitution of these expressions into the displayed triple is formal; no geometric classification is certified.

For lambda!=0 the fractional map g(z)=lambda/z satisfies g(g(z))=z and its finite fixed points satisfy z^2=lambda. It interchanges0 and infinity, so it cannot fix P=0 in unchanged coordinates. The surrounding calculation is cancelled and may have changed coordinates; retain the ink and flag this limitation rather than repairing it.
